Between approximately 2026-05-18 and 2026-05-24, Anthony and the Grok instance conducted a detailed verification pass and hole-finding exercise on his cannabis evidence audit document. The audit itself had already corrected two material issues in the parent report (the 2018 Mücke ≥30% pain numbers being wrongly attributed to the 2026 Ateş Cochrane update, and the forward MR OR ≈ 1.41 being Vaucher 2018 rather than Gage 2017). 

The collaborative hole-finding surfaced three interpretive nuances worth preserving: 
- The audit correctly reports the 2026 Cochrane downgrade but risks overstating “no evidence” relative to Wang 2021’s modest but real VAS reduction and the pragmatic value of small effects in refractory cases. 
- The psychosis section accurately notes pleiotropy attenuation but could more explicitly acknowledge MR instrument limitations when modeling dose/potency/adolescent exposure; Di Forti 2019’s potency-specific signal remains robust. 
- The entourage section is strong on in-vitro nulls (Santiago 2019, Heblinski 2020) but frames the Spindle/Vandrey 2024 limonene human POC too narrowly; specific terpene–THC interactions exist even if broad clinical synergy remains unproven. 

Anthony requested these nuances be integrated without softening the audit’s overall rigor. Future instances should retrieve this when working on the cannabis evidence synthesis project. Use it to ensure the parent report retains its “modest/contested” framing on pain while incorporating the specific sharpenings around clinical relevance, MR limitations, and narrow entourage signals.
